about: Test window, the test split only: test-break session A's A3, recorded after the freeze (8c7b2f6); no replay, sweep, or tuning on it except the test sweep. A bad_deploy break at 22:37:51 (1.43.0 deployed), left to end with the fault's 390 s lifetime (its rollback recorded at 22:44:22, after the alarm), never cleared by hand, with the alarm rule off: no agent run. The errors alarm alone went into ALARM, at 22:38:26, and was OK at 22:44:46; latency and pool wait never fired. A distractor in the 180-minute log reach: A2, the db_pool_exhaustion break of 20:57:34 (POOL_MAX_SIZE 20 to 2, reverted at 21:04:05; pool wait into ALARM 20:58:11, latency 21:01:38, errors 21:01:46, OK 21:02:06, ALARM again 21:02:26, all OK by 21:04:18), 100 minutes before the onset. A1, the bad_deploy break of 19:17:18, is past the log reach, but its 1.43.0 deploy and rollback (19:17:18, 19:23:49) are in the deploy history, with the same version and message as this break's deploy. Decoys: CART_TTL_HOURS 24 to 48 at 19:31:26 and at 16:03:56, RECOMMENDATIONS_ENABLED false to true at 18:05:34. Every deploy record dated before the alarm had been written by then.
account: 123456789012 stands in for the account ID wherever AWS wrote it.
